stem: Which of the following best describes the function of the cerebral aqueduct:
options: Major site of production of CSF
Connects the lateral ventricles to the third ventricle
Drains CSF into the subarachnoid cisterns
Connects the third ventricle to the fourth ventricle
Connects the right and left lateral ventricles
fact: The cerebral aqueduct connects the third and fourth ventricles.
finding: Displayed key and option order directly verified on the original rendered page.

stem: What type of visual field defect would you most likely see in a lesion of the optic radiation of the left temporal lobe:
fact: A left temporal Meyer-loop lesion causes a right homonymous superior quadrantanopia.
finding: Displayed key and option order directly verified on the original rendered page.

stem: What type of visual field defect are you most likely to see in a lesion of the optic nerve:
fact: An optic-nerve lesion causes ipsilateral monocular visual loss.
finding: Displayed key and option order directly verified on the original rendered page.

stem: Which of the following clinical features is most suggestive of a lesion of the occipital lobe:
fact: A unilateral occipital lesion can cause homonymous hemianopia.
finding: Displayed key and option order directly verified on the original rendered page.

stem: The blood supply to the occipital lobe is primarily supplied from which of the following arteries:
fact: The PCA primarily supplies the occipital lobe, with additional MCA supply near the occipital pole.
finding: Displayed key and option order directly verified on the original rendered page; source caveat retained.

stem: The substantia nigra is located in which of the following regions of the brain:
fact: The substantia nigra is a midbrain nucleus.
finding: Displayed key and option order directly verified on the original rendered page.

stem: Which of the following clinical features is most suggestive of a lesion of the frontal lobe:
options: Conjugate eye deviation towards the side of the lesion
fact: Frontal-eye-field damage can cause conjugate gaze deviation toward the lesion.
mnemonic: Frontal eye field: eyes face the lesion.
finding: Displayed key and option order directly verified on the original rendered page.

stem: The blood supply to the parietal lobe is primarily supplied by which of the following arteries:
fact: The middle cerebral artery supplies much of the lateral parietal cortex.

stem: A 65 year old lady presents to ED complaining of visual loss. Examination demonstrates visual loss in the lower left quadrant in both visual fields. The lesion would most likely be in which of the following:
fact: A right parietal optic-radiation lesion causes left inferior homonymous quadrantanopia.
finding: Displayed key and option order directly verified on the original rendered page.

stem: The corpus callosum is composed of which type of fibres:
fact: The corpus callosum is a commissural fibre system linking the cerebral hemispheres.
